title: Metro returns to Singapore homes with Wing Tai at Dunearn Road, to exit its department stores
article:
Mainboard-listed Metro Holdings swung to a pre-tax profit of $5.9 million for the first half of FY2027 ended Sept 30, as it returned to Singapore's residential market and prepared to exit its two department stores here.

The return to profit, from a pre-tax loss of $12.9 million a year earlier, was mainly due to smaller fair value losses on China investment properties held through associates and joint ventures. Revenue rose 51.6% to $63.1 million from $41.6 million. Net gearing stood at 0.28 times, with cash and short-term investments of $325.4 million.

"We will continue to focus on proactive asset management to strengthen our portfolio, optimise returns, and seek new opportunities for capital redeployment," says Metro group CEO Yip Hoong Mun.

Metro won the 99-year leasehold Dunearn Road site in a government land sale (GLS) tender in May, in a 30:70 joint venture with Wing Tai Holdings . The partners paid $533 million, or $1,625 psf per plot ratio (ppr), and plan to develop a 330-unit residential project with up to 1,400 sqm (15,070 sq ft) of ground-floor commercial space, including a childcare centre of at least 600 sqm (6,460 sq ft).

The site is in the upcoming Bukit Timah Turf City precinct in District 10, next to the Swiss Club Good Class Bungalow (GCB) Area. Metro has so far funded $77.6 million towards its 30% stake, according to its 1HFY2027 results released on Nov 13.

It is Metro's first residential GLS win since 2012, when it teamed up with Wing Tai and Maxdin, a unit of the former UE E&C, for the Prince Charles Crescent site. The 469-unit project, The Crest , was completed in 2017.

VisionCrest Orchard, an 11-storey freehold commercial development on Penang Road in prime District 9, was acquired for $450 million in November 2023 by a joint venture of Metro (20%), TE Capital Partners and LaSalle Investment Management, which then sub-divided the units for strata sale.

The last office unit was sold for $7.6 million ($4,358 psf) in June, according to a caveat lodged.

Metro, which started as a textile shop at 72 High Street in 1957, will also stop running its department stores at Metro Paragon and Metro Causeway Point when the existing leases end.

The group announced the move on July 20, after a strategic review of its retail business, and plans to shift to smaller multi-concept stores. It is in talks with existing and other landlords.

Its brand management arm, Grand Brands Asia, opened its first two labels, Gentlewoman and LSOUL, at 313@Somerset in October.

Retail revenue slipped to $37.0 million from $38.8 million a year earlier, while the segment loss narrowed to $1.6 million from $3.7 million.

Asia Green, Metro's 50%-owned office towers at Tampines Regional Centre, was about 90.0% occupied, down from 93.7% a year earlier.

Overseas, China remains Metro's largest property exposure. Occupancy at Metro City and Metro Tower in Shanghai and GIE Tower in Guangzhou averaged 72.6%, down from 73.9%. Metro Tower was just 51.7% occupied, against 70.8% at GIE Tower and 95.4% at Metro City.

In Indonesia, Metro sold all 1,471 units in Tower 5 of its Bekasi development, lifting property division revenue to $26.1 million from $2.9 million. In Manchester, Metro has sold or reserved 132 of the 189 units at Railings, the third phase of the 50%-owned Middlewood Locks, with the other 57 kept for lease.

In Australia, Metro's 30%-owned portfolio with Sim Lian , comprising 17 freehold office and retail assets valued at about A$1.4 billion, was 94.9% occupied.

title: Smart Look At The Week Ahead: NVIDIA, Alibaba, Walt Disney And Walmart
article:
The only central bank of note to announce its latest interest-rate decision will be the People’s Bank of China. In October, the central bank kept its one-year loan prime rate at a record low of 3.0%.
The Chinese economy seems to be growing with interest rates where they are. So, additional support is probably unnecessary, at this time. Additionally, the housing market is still under pressure. So, no change is expected to the five-year loan prime rate, too.
Meanwhile, the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit will take place in Shenzhen. Reportedly Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin will meet on the sidelines at the conference. Who knows what they will talk about. An end to the wars between Russia and Ukraine, and the U.S. and Iran would be a good place start. But don’t hold your breath.
On the corporate front
There is probably only one set of results that really matters next week.
NVIDIA
(Nasdaq: NVDA) will report third-quarter results without Jensen Huang at the helm. Interim CEO Colette Kress will be in the hot seat as the chip designer reports a doubling of profit and revenue. But will that be enough to reverse a 30% drop in the company’s share price?
Staying with tech issues,
Alibaba
(NYSE: BABA) is expected to report a considerably more modest growth in earnings and revenue in the high single digits. But investors will be scrutinising growth its cloud business, especially if America should tighten the export of chips to China following the fallout from the NVIDIA debacle.
There are also results from a trio of popular Chinese Internet companies, namely,
Baidu
(Nasdaq: BIDU),
JD.com
(SEHK: 9618) and
PDD Holdings
(Nasdaq: PDD). Search engine Baidu is pinning its hopes on AI, as its traditional online marketing and advertising revenues are declining. Meanwhile, online retailers JD.com and PDD are facing sluggish domestic demand and competition.
The Walt Disney Company
(NYSE: DIS) is expected to post a strong increase in earnings on revenue that grew modestly. Disney should have a lot to crow about – revenue from Toy Story 5 has crossed the billion-dollar mark. But attendance at its theme parks have been easing.
Other companies pencilled in for results include car maker Chinese
XPeng
(SEHK: 9868), home-improvement retailer
The Home Depot
(NYSE: HD), supermarket owner
Walmart
(NYSE: WMT) and online travel agency
Trip.com
(SEHK: 9961).

title: US flight chaos persists with thousands of cancellations, delays
article:
(Nov 14): US air travel struggled to recover on Saturday from the longest nationwide flight suspension since the September 2001 terrorist attacks, with thousands of cancellations following an outage that laid bare the fragility of America’s aviation infrastructure.

Airlines are rushing to restore regular schedules, leaving about 3,500 flights into, out of, and especially within the US cancelled and 1,200 trips delayed on Saturday as of 7.15am New York time, according to aviation data firm FlightAware. Some 22,200 domestic and international US-linked flights are scheduled to depart US airports on Saturday, with about 14% of scheduled flights cancelled, Cirium data shows.

“Operations are slowly returning to normal this morning,” Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said in a post on X. “You will continue to see some delays and cancellations as carriers reschedule flights and reposition aircraft/crews where they are needed most.”

The disruption followed a nationwide halt to flight movements on Friday — only the third in US history — after the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) imposed a ground stop that lasted for more than four hours. Some 3,500 aircraft in the sky dwindled to less than 400 as authorities blamed a data overload for crippling air traffic control communications and radar.

The failure left airlines trying to rebuild schedules with aircraft and crew scattered and out of position after take-offs were suspended on Friday afternoon, while also dealing with hundreds of thousands of passengers who’d been stranded on tarmacs and stuck in terminals.

See also: SIA says it will review feedback and explore ‘further refinements’ after cabin refresh launch

American Airlines Group Inc, the US’s biggest carrier by fleet size, warned of residual delays and cancellations as it worked to get aircraft and crew to the right locations. The Dallas-based carrier said it was “positioning the airline for the strongest possible recovery” on Saturday and in the days ahead.

Delta Air Lines Inc said “it will take time to reset our operation, including the positioning of aircraft and crews”.

Other US carriers, including JetBlue Airways Corp and United Airlines Holding Inc, warned of similar ongoing disruptions to schedules into Saturday, and encouraged passengers who didn’t urgently need to travel to consider rescheduling.

See also: ST Engineering wins initial 'low rate' order for land system platform from defence customer in Europe

Delta’s mainline services saw 631 cancellations, or 20% of its daily schedule. JetBlue has seen 335 flights culled, two-fifths of its departures, according to FlightAware data, while American scrapped 431 trips, about 15% of its daily schedule.

Duffy told reporters on Friday night that it would “take time” to unwind the impact from Friday, but expected the system to “be back up and operational as we come into the heat of travel during Thanksgiving” later this month.

Aviation officials and airlines were confronted with a cocktail of failing technology and an ageing system. The breakdown comes amid a politically-charged effort to overhaul and modernise, at high cost, the ailing infrastructure that underpins the communications and tracking system of aircraft in the US.

Duffy called for Congress to fund an emergency US$50 billion upgrade to complete the modernisation effort. He’d previously asked for an additional US$30 billion in the days prior to the latest breakdown.

The transport chief stood side-by-side with Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin at the White House to spell out how outdated equipment, running over capacity and already not coping well, had been pushed to breaking point.

Mullin told reporters that the FAA was “putting patches into the system” and the new technology was “overwhelming the older system”.

Key pieces of equipment, already running over capacity and struggling to cope, were overwhelmed Friday, according to an FAA briefing to the industry that was described to Bloomberg by people familiar with the matter. The failure cascaded and impacted the backbone of the FAA’s old telecoms system that handles voice and data information that is used by air traffic controllers and pilots, the people said.

Specific locations were affected, however, and L3Harris Technologies Inc, which operates and helps maintains the older telecommunications network, is being tasked to diagnose the cause of the data overload, the people said. The US aerospace and defence firm did not respond to a request for comment outside of regular business hours.

Duffy sought to reassure air travelers it’s safe to fly — insisting the US has “the safest system in the world” — even as he couldn’t rule out a similar air traffic control outage happening in the future.

“Is this exact thing going to happen again? I don’t know that this exact scenario will happen,” he said.

title: Zelenskyy: US floats Donbas for Russia, Nato membership for Ukraine
article:
(Nov 14): Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said US peace envoys asked whether Ukraine would be willing to give up the Donbas region in the nation’s east to Russia in exchange for Nato membership, signalling a potential shift in Washington’s negotiating tactics.

As the full-scale war between Ukraine and Russia heads towards the end of its fifth year in February with no end in sight, the administration of US President Donald Trump is trying to make a breakthrough in the peace negotiations they are moderating.

“It was the first time this had been raised,” Zelenskyy told reporters in his office in Kyiv late on Friday of the plan involving the large Donestsk and Luhansk regions. “We are discussing with our partners a comprehensive security package that could be offered to us in the negotiations.”

Zelenskyy said that the package floated by Washington includes specific security guarantees from Nato and the European Union, a strong Ukrainian army, meaning an adequate number of troops, weapons, and financial support for a specified period of time, as well as a recovery plan backed by funding with clearly identified sources.

“If the American side confirms precisely this to us, together with other Nato partners, then I will ask our Ukrainian society what it thinks: do we accept it or not?” Zelenskyy said. “I have no right to make that decision on my own.”

Zelenskyy said Kyiv is looking for security guarantees modelled on Article 5 of the North Atlantic Treaty Organization as an “absolute minimum”. The US officials responded that “it could be something similar to Articles 4 and 5 of Nato”, Zelenskyy said, adding that Ukraine needs more clarity.

See also: Apple fined £390,000 by UK over Russian sanction breaches

“My question to the American side was, ‘If you give us this something similar to Nato, will American soldiers be on our soil?’” Zelenskyy said. “Their answer was ‘no’.”

The US idea was based on bilateral security guarantees, similar to what Israel has, Ukraine’s leader said.

Earlier this week, US envoys Jared Kushner, Trump’s son in law, and Steve Witkoff met with their Ukrainian and Russian counterparts in Abu Dhabi for talks that yielded some progress, according to all sides. While Kyiv and Moscow agreed to a substantial exchange of prisoners of war, territorial disputes remain far from resolved.

See also: Putin declares new 72-hour Ukraine truce to mark WWII victory

At a subsequent meeting in Moscow on Thursday, Russian President Vladimir Putin told Witkoff and Kushner that the presence of foreign troops in Ukraine would threaten Russia’s security and was unacceptable. The Kremlin has long argued that Nato’s expansion into Eastern Europe after the collapse of the Soviet Union threatens Russian security, and has cited it as one of the reasons for its 2022 invasion of Ukraine.

Russia also agreed to allow EU representatives to join the talks. The bloc is expected to decide on its envoys by the end of this month, Zelenskyy said.

Meanwhile, Kyiv faces what it sees as periodic pressure from Washington to accept unfavourable peace terms. The latest example is restrictions on the use of Starshield, a satellite-based communications system developed by Elon Musk’s SpaceX for military purposes.

Zelenskyy said Starshield terminals are currently restricted in Russian-occupied areas of Ukraine, hampering Kyiv’s air defences, which attempt to intercept Russian drones and missiles before they reach other parts of the country.
